Classification and constraints\n12\t- **What:** one line on the system.\n13\t- **Type:** software / infra / AI-agentic (or a mix); greenfield or brownfield; small build or not.\n14\t- **Dominant constraint:** correctness | availability | latency | cost | scale | compliance.\n15\t- **Worst failure:** the single failure that would hurt most.\n16\t\n17\t**Budgets** (only the rows that bind; add rows the system needs, such as a cutover freeze window):\n18\t\n19\t| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n20\t|---|---|---|---|\n21\t| Latency | … | REQUIREMENT / BASELINE / ASSUMPTION / UNKNOWN | V… or Phase … |\n22\t| Throughput | … | … | … |\n23\t| Availability / SLO | … | … | … |\n24\t| RPO / RTO | … | … | … |\n25\t| Resource use | … | … | … |\n26\t| AI inference cost | … (AI systems only) | … | … |\n27\t| Storage cost | … | … | … |\n28\t| Operational complexity | … (e.g. services to run, on-call load) | … | … |\n29\t\n30\tAn UNKNOWN target has no number: write the missing input, who supplies it, and the phase that\n31\tneeds it. An ASSUMPTION gives its basis.\n32\t\n33\t**Missing inputs:** the unknowns that would change the plan most, and any assumption the phase\n34\torder rests on.\n35\t\n36\t## 2. Dependency map\n37\tOnly the dependencies that bind and that the phase order does not already show:\n38\t\n39\t| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n40\t|---|---|---|---|\n41\t| … | … | decision / validation / risk-security / organizational / economic (structural or runtime only when surprising) | built / deployed / specified / hardened / exposed / committed |\n42\t\n43\tThen one line naming the kinds with no instance (\"No organizational or economic dependencies.\").\n44\tIn brownfield work, mark each dependency CONFIRMED or ASSUMED.\n45\t\n46\t## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n47\t\n48\t| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n49\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n50\t| Consistency vs availability | R2/R3 + one-clause reason | … | … | V…, a cheap check, or the cited basis | … (for a gated row: \"V… fails, or …\") |\n51\t| Monolith vs services | … | … | … | … | … |\n52\t| Sync vs async | … | … | … | … | … |\n53\t| Build vs buy | … | … | … | … | … |\n54\t| Data-privacy boundary (personal or regulated data) | … | … | … | … | … |\n55\t| <each system-specific R2/R3 decision, e.g. the tenancy model> | … | … | … | … | … |\n56\t| (Brownfield) migration strategy, coexistence and cutover, rollback, system of record | … | … | … | … | … |\n57\t| (AI) prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | … | … | … | … | … |\n58\t| (AI) hosted API vs self-host | … | … | … | … | … |\n59\t\n60\t**R1 defaults:** <decision> → <default>; … (one line; no rows for R1 decisions).\n61\t**N/A:** <considered decisions that do not apply> — <reason> (one line).\n62\tOmit the (Brownfield) and (AI) rows when they do not apply. Inherited brownfield decisions the\n63\tplan will not change are listed once as constraints, not as rows.\n64\t\n65\t## 4. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n66\t- The one real request and the real response.\n67\t- Every tier it crosses.\n68\t- How it is deployed, logged, monitored, and rolled back on day zero.\n69\t- Who can reach it (internal or allow-listed traffic behind a flag until its controls exist).\n70\t\n71\tIf an exception changes Phase 0, say so in one line and cite it (E…).\n72\tExit check (V0): a real request succeeds with one trace across every tier; a deploy and a\n73\trollback succeed through the pipeline; an injected failure fires an alert; the first values of\n74\tthe measurable budgets are recorded as baselines, not targets.\n75\t\n76\t## 5. Phases (Phase 1 onward; dependency order; within a phase, rework widest first, exposure smallest first)\n77\tFor each phase:\n78\t- **Phase N — <name>**\n79\t  - Unlocks: what becomes possible after it.\n80\t  - Depends on: earlier phases and V-IDs, by reference.\n81\t  - Tasks: in order.\n82\t  - Rollback: how this phase is undone, or its point of no return and the gate that guards it.\n83\t  - Exit check: its gates pass, plus any observable condition that no gate covers.\n84\t\n85\t## 6. Cross-cutting concerns (per phase, from the first commit)\n96\t\n97\t| Phase | Security | Observability | Reproducibility | Resilience |\n98\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n99\t| 0 | … | … | … | … |\n100\t\n101\tObservability appears in Phase 0. No cell is empty; where a declared exception bypasses one, cite\n102\tit (E…).\n103\t\n104\t## 8. AI layer (AI/agentic systems only)\n105\t\n106\t| Sublayer | In this system | Built in | Exit check or V-ID |\n107\t|---|---|---|---|\n108\t| 1. Classification and constraints\n- **What:** A local command-line tool. It reads each photo's EXIF capture date and renames the file to a sortable, date-based name. It can preview the changes first (dry run) and undo them afterwards.\n- **Type:** Software. Greenfield. A small build: one developer, no outside service, no money flow, and no regulated data. Photos do contain personal data such as GPS location, but they never leave the machine.\n- **Dominant constraint:** Correctness.\n- **Worst failure:** A rename overwrites or loses a photo, which may be the only copy. Close behind it: a partial run leaves the folder half-renamed with no way back.\n\n**Budgets**\n\n| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Data integrity | 0 files lost or overwritten; file count and file bytes are the same after a run as before | REQUIREMENT (the request says \"renames\": a rename keeps every file and its bytes) | V1, V3 |\n| Recovery | One `undo <run-id>` restores every original name after a run that finished or was interrupted | ASSUMPTION (basis: without undo, a mistake is permanent) | V1 |\n| Throughput | 10,000 photos planned and renamed in ≤ 2 min on a local SSD | ASSUMPTION (basis: ExifTool in batch mode reads headers at hundreds of files per second, and a typical phone dump is a few thousand files). The baseline is recorded in V0. SD cards and network drives will be slower | Phase 1 exit |\n| Operational complexity | No services to run; one pipx package plus ExifTool on the user's PATH | ASSUMPTION (that users can install ExifTool; confirm with you) | V0 |\n\n**Missing inputs** (none of these change the phase order):\n1. **Formats in scope.** JPEG only, or also HEIC, RAW (CR2/CR3/NEF/ARW/DNG), or video? You supply this; Phase 1 needs it to build the V2 test set. Default: JPEG and HEIC.\n2. **Sidecars and catalogs.** Do you use `.xmp` sidecars, iPhone `.aae` edit files, Live Photo `.mov` pairs, or a Lightroom or Apple Photos catalog? Renaming files that a catalog manages breaks the catalog's links. You supply this; Phase 1 needs it.\n3. **Operating systems and filesystems.** Windows, macOS, Linux? exFAT SD cards? NAS or SMB shares? This sets the V1 test matrix. Default: all three OSes, plus exFAT.\n4. **Naming and time-zone preference.** Default: camera-local time with no time-zone conversion.\n\n## 2. Dependency map\n\n| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `apply` mode (any real rename) | V1: no-overwrite rename, journal, undo | risk/security | exposed (to real photos) |\n| List of supported formats; naming rules for HEIC and RAW | Missing input 1; V2 | decision / validation | specified |\n| Sidecar and Live Photo handling | Missing input 2 | decision | specified |\n| Running `apply` on your real library | A verified backup you have made; V3 | organizational / risk | exposed |\n| Every run | ExifTool installed where the CLI runs (an unusual runtime dependency) | runtime | deployed |\n\nThere are no economic dependencies.\n\n## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n\n| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| How renames are executed, and what stays consistent | R3: if wrong, photos are overwritten, which cannot be undone | 1. Build the whole plan first. 2. Detect collisions inside the plan and against files already in the folder, including names that differ only by letter case. 3. Write each journal entry and flush it to disk before doing that rename. 4. Rename each file atomically without ever overwriting: hard-link then unlink on POSIX, `os.rename` on Windows (it fails if the target exists). Where hard links aren't supported (exFAT), check that the target doesn't exist, then rename. 5. The batch as a whole is not atomic; undo and resume cover a partial run | No other process writes to the folder during a run. Each primitive refuses to overwrite on every target filesystem | V1 | V1 fails on some filesystem. Then on that filesystem, either refuse `apply` or switch to copy, verify the hash, then delete |\n| Naming scheme and date source | R2: once users have renamed whole libraries, changing the scheme means renaming them all again | Name format `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.ext`: hyphens because Windows forbids colons, and the original extension is kept. Date from `DateTimeOriginal`, then `CreateDate`, otherwise skip and report the file. Camera-local time. Same-second collisions get `_01`, `_02`, … in `SubSecTimeOriginal` order, then by original name. Files already named correctly are left alone | You want chronological names, and a file with no EXIF date should be left alone rather than guessed | V2; your sign-off on the dry-run sample in V3 | You want UTC or the offset in the name, or a fallback to file modification time |\n| Data-privacy boundary | R3: EXIF holds GPS location, and leaked location can't be taken back | Fully local and no network code. The log and journal record only paths and the date tags used, never GPS or other EXIF. Test photos have GPS stripped (`exiftool -gps:all=`) before they are committed | Nothing needs the network | Cited basis: the code has no network path. It becomes opt-in and gets its own gate |\n\n**R1 defaults:**\n- Language and distribution: Python 3.11+, installed with pipx or `uv tool`, wheels built by GitHub Actions with trusted publishing.\n- EXIF reader: use ExifTool rather than writing a parser, via one `exiftool -json` batch call, behind a `MetadataReader` interface.\n- Default mode: dry run; real renames need `--apply` plus a confirmation prompt.\n- Scope: the top-level folder only.\n\n**N/A:**\n- Monolith vs services: it's one process.\n- Sync vs async: it's sequential local I/O, and ExifTool batching covers throughput.\n- Consistency vs availability: there is no distributed state; per-file consistency is covered in the first row.\n- Brownfield and AI rows: greenfield, no AI component.\n\n## 4. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n- **The one real request:** `photorename ~/Pictures/2024-trip`, a dry run on one real folder.\n- **The response:**\n  - a table of planned renames, e.g. `IMG_0412.JPG → 2024-07-14_09-31-02.JPG`;\n  - skipped files with reasons;\n  - a summary line such as `412 planned, 3 skipped (no EXIF date), 0 conflicts`;\n  - the exit code;\n  - the path of the run log.\n- **Tiers it crosses:**\n  1. argument parsing;\n  2. folder scan;\n  3. ExifTool subprocess;\n  4. name planner;\n  5. reporter (screen output and a log in the per-user state folder, located with `platformdirs`);\n  6. executor, stubbed read-only. It refuses to rename, because the guard (V1) doesn't exist yet.\n- **Deploy:** pushing tag `v0.0.1` makes GitHub Actions run the tests and publish the wheel. The tool is installed with `pipx install` on clean Windows, macOS, and Linux CI runners and on your machine.\n- **Rollback:** reinstall the previous version (`pipx install photorename==<prev>`) and yank the bad release. Rehearsed once, from `v0.0.2` back to `v0.0.1`.\n- **Logging and monitoring:** whoever runs the tool sees the result directly:\n  - every log starts with a run ID, the tool version, and the ExifTool version;\n  - errors on individual files are counted and reported, and the run continues;\n  - exit code 2 if any file errored, 3 if ExifTool is missing.\n- **Who can reach it:** you and the developer only, through a pre-release version. Phases\n\n- **Phase 1: Safe apply and undo**\n  - Unlocks: real renames (`--apply`) and `undo`.\n  - Depends on: Phase 0 (V0); missing inputs 1–3.\n  - Tasks, in order (widest blast radius first):\n    1.
